title: Which number is greater in each pair of powers?
description: Three pairs of numbers made with powers are compared: four cubed with three to the power four, two to the power eight with eight squared, and one hundred squared with two to the power one hundred. Small powers are worked out, and the huge one is compared with a power we can work out.
teaching_notes: One idea: compare powers by working out the small ones and, for a huge one, setting it against a power that can be worked out. Watch for students who think the bigger base always wins.

video_script.why: A bigger base does not always give a bigger number. Working out the powers, or comparing with a known power, settles each pair.
video_script.substitution: Work out each small power; for the huge one, compare it with a power that can be worked out.
video_script.anchor: three pairs of numbers made with powers
video_script.payoff_line: Work out the small powers, and compare the huge one with a power you know

final_answer.value: 3⁴, 2 to the power 8 and 2 to the power 100
final_answer.spoken: In the first pair, three to the power four is greater. In the second pair, two to the power eight is greater. In the third pair, two to the power one hundred is greater.

video_script.design: Each pair sits in a row. The values of the small powers appear beside them. The huge power is set against 2¹⁴ on a short bar.

marks.s1: 4³ = 64 and 3⁴ = 81 are written side by side

narration: <bookmark mark='s1'/>Step one, the first pair.
Four cubed is sixty four, and three to the power four is eighty one.

marks.s2: 2⁸ = 256 and 8² = 64 are written side by side

narration: <bookmark mark='s2'/>Step two, the second pair.
Two to the power eight is two hundred fifty six, and eight squared is sixty four.

narration: <bookmark mark='s3'/>Step three, the third pair.
One hundred squared is ten thousand.
<bookmark mark='fourteen'/>Two to the power fourteen is sixteen thousand three hundred eighty four.
<bookmark mark='more'/>Two to the power one hundred is more than two to the power fourteen.

marks.again: the check lines for 2⁸ and 2¹⁴ are written below it

narration: <bookmark mark='s4'/>Step four, check the values another way.
Nine times nine is eighty one, which is three to the power four.
<bookmark mark='again'/>Sixteen times sixteen is two hundred fifty six.
One hundred twenty eight times one hundred twenty eight is sixteen thousand three hundred eighty four.
